chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Habib al-Khath'ami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not inform you of the best among you?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Those with the best character, those who are amiable and hospitable, and those who get along with people and with whom others get along well.'

key_terms.الْمَوْطُؤُونَ أَكْنَافًا: Those who are amiable/easy to be around (literally: those whose sides are trodden upon, implying humility)
key_terms.يُؤْلِفُونَ وَيُؤْلَفُونَ: Those who foster affection and are reciprocated with it

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the best people according to the Prophet in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) redefines excellence through the lens of social humility and emotional intelligence, emphasizing that true leadership is manifested in approachability rather than authority. The term 'al-mawtu'una aknafan' (those easy to be around) reflects the Shia ideal of *tawadu'* (humility), where the righteous lower themselves to connect with others, fostering a community bound by mutual affection (*alif wa ifa*). This narration underscores the practical application of moral character in daily interactions, aligning with the Imams' teachings on softening one's demeanor to win hearts.
